overall: The AG found the Townsend Housing Authority Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of three allegations: outside discussion of draft minutes, minutes revisions, and dropping a notice topic.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly discussed and revised its September 18, 2017 draft minutes outside of a posted meeting.
Revised minutes allegedly omitted a reference to a veterans' focus group report that was described in the original draft as attached.
allegations.key_passage: Absent evidence to the contrary, we credit the Board's account and find that the revised meeting minutes accurately reflect the Board's discussion during the meeting.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly dropped the veterans focus group topic from the October 27, 2017 meeting notice after it had been listed on the October 23 notice.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by omitting this topic on its October 27, 2017 meeting notice where it did not discuss the topic during the meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
